title: Enclosing Schema
strapline: Fences round the farm animals, a border round the drawing, a wall round themselves — the child who builds boundaries.
intent: Recognise enclosing as a schema — the drive to build borders, fences, walls and edges, and to be inside enclosed spaces.
Understand the learning inside it: inside and outside, boundary, area, and the difference a wall makes.
Read the fenced-in animals, the boxed-off drawing and the den built round the body as spatial research.
Build construction skills and spatial reasoning through walling, bordering and surrounding.
Support the emotional pull of the enclosed space too — a den or a boundary can feel wonderfully safe.
implementation: Offer building materials that make boundaries: blocks, bricks, fences, loops of string, hoops, tape, dens and tunnels.
Provide small-world enclosures — farm and zoo animals with fences, cars with a garage, people with a house wall.
Name the schema as you play ('you've built a wall all the way round — the animals are safe inside').
Add drawing and mark-making, and notice the child who rings their marks with a firm border.
Offer real dens and cosy enclosed corners, honouring the urge to be inside a boundary of one's own.
key_questions: Who is safe inside your wall?
Is there a way in and out, or is it all closed up?
Shall we build a fence right around the farm?
You've drawn a line all the way round — what's inside it?
Can you fit inside the den you've made?

impact.text: A child builds walls, fences and borders, exploring inside and outside and what a boundary keeps in or out.
Toddlers place and balance bricks and fences into enclosures, construction and spatial skills growing as they build.
Enclosing feeds pretend — animals fenced safe, a house walled round the dolls, a den to hide inside.
Children explore space directly — inside, outside, around, within — building and stepping into their own boundaries.

enhancements: Farm and zoo small-world with plenty of fencing to build enclosures.
Blocks and bricks in quantity for walls that go all the way round.
Hoops, loops of rope and tape to mark boundaries on the floor.
Big boxes, dens and tunnels for enclosing the whole body.
Mark-making with an invitation to draw a border round the page.

playing_exploring: The child builds and inhabits enclosures on their own terms, deciding what goes inside.
Boundaries are explored hands-on, in construction and in whole-body dens.
active_learning: Toddlers rebuild a wall each time it falls, working to close the boundary all the way round.
creating_thinking: Children hold an idea of inside and outside and build to make it real — a safe space with an edge.
